ev.q: The category percentage concordance (overlap) across the four countries was calculated by dividing the number of criteria used by all countries
The proportion of fever-dependent criteria for the community alert category declined from 56% at the start of the outbreak to 30%
Concordance in the criteria for case contact remained consistently low, increasing from 17% to 20%
By the end of the 6 months, the suspected category included a higher proportion of fever-dependent criteria (65%)
Concordance in the criteria for case contact remained consistently low, increasing from 17% to 20% over the 6-month period
Except for the case contact and confirmed categories, all countries included more criteria per category than did the WHO definitions.
Three dates for comparison were chosen to assess definitions
Changes in MOH-approved Ebola case definitions were analyzed, referencing the WHO standard case definition

methods_quotes.q: The category percentage concordance (overlap) across the four countries was calculated by dividing the number of criteria used by all countries
The number of criteria present for each country was divided by the total number of possible criteria listed by all of the four countries
Countries that did not use a category were excluded from that category’s analysis.
